question: Jason's finding first: he saw an action commanded in the wrong state (Z move in the gripper-close state) in the generated PnP. Which rung exactly? The agent's self-checks compare code against the diagram — this case becomes a permanent automated check.
What's the acceptance test for generated code — what makes you trust it enough to run on a machine, beyond importing clean?
Wideband policy: which transitions may early-advance, in one rule? (Current guess: only when the next motion can't collide with the settling axis.)
Manual servo speeds: manual/jog rungs read Accel[0]/Decel[0] (shared with auto) in the template. Intentional, or should manual have its own indices?
Init-with-part: templates re-enter mid-sequence when a part is already gripped at power-up (124 + GripperClosed). What's the general rule for choosing the re-entry state on any new station?
Fault vs warning: the rule for which conditions fault (stop) vs warn (q_Pause)? "Waiting for upstream" = warning — what else?
q_ActuatorsSafe: the precise definition per station type. All actuators home? Or a defined safe subset per application?
Homing: when torque-home (AOI_TorqueHome) vs MAH? Who decides, and what marks a station as needing homing before auto?
HMI_Toggle vs Tracking OpStatus: V4.2 sources Lockout/DryRun/SS from \Tracking...OpStatus. Is HMI_Toggle officially dead in new programs?
Where should the agent ask vs. decide? Before generating, it asks a short list (devices, transitions, timeouts, handshakes). What must ALWAYS be asked, and what may it default?

What Z height (mm from Retract = 0) clears the pick nest, the place nest, and any surrounding fixtures, so the horizontal axis may start moving while Z is still rising? That value becomes the AOI_RangeCheck wide deadband on ZAxisRetract (the rounded-corner threshold and the X-axis permissive) — the template default of 5 mm is almost certainly too tight.

question: Trigger and acquisition mechanics, per camera family we actually buy (Cognex/Keyence/other): how does the PLC trigger — hardwired output, EtherNet/IP assembly bit, or explicit message? And is 'result ready' one handshake or two (acquisition complete vs. evaluation complete)? I want to model the handshake correctly per family instead of assuming the legacy four-wire q_Trigger/i_TrigRdy/i_ResultReady/i_InspPass shape everywhere.

When does a vision application send coordinates versus just pass/fail? What's the judgment — is it purely 'a downstream motion needs correction', or are there cases where we take coordinates anyway (drift monitoring, SPC)? And when coordinates ARE sent, who consumes them — servo target offset, robot frame shift, or operator display only?

Where does vision result data live, by convention? Part tracking gets the boolean (and numerics like X_Offset in Molex), but what about the raw job outputs — do we keep a per-camera or per-job UDT, copy from the input assembly into named tags, or read on demand? What's the naming/structure you'd want a new hire to follow?

Motion overlap during exposure: what's the rule for what may move while the camera is exposing? Dial locked (shot pin / IndexComplete) before imaging a dial-mounted part is obvious — but do we ever image during motion (flying trigger), and how do you choose the settle time before the trigger versus the legacy fixed 50 ms dwell?

State structure per vision mode: the legacy convention compiled every inspection into 4 sub-states (verify trigger ready → settle dwell → trigger → check results). Does that skeleton hold for job-select and coordinate-feedback applications, or do those genuinely need different/extra states (job load + acknowledge, offset transfer + accept)? What's the state anatomy you'd draw for each mode?

Retry vs. route vs. fault on a failed inspection: when is a fail just 'record FAILURE to part tracking and let the reject station sort it' versus 'retry the trigger (bounded by search timeout)' versus 'fault the station'? Is the driver the process (can a retry change the answer?), the part cost, or line policy — and who sets the retry count?

Mode selection judgment: given a new motion requirement, how do you decide between electronic gearing, point-to-point (MAM), and blended point-to-point? Is gearing strictly for continuously-synchronized axes (follower tied to a master), or do we also use it where a chassis/cam would have been used mechanically? A decision tree in your words is what I'm after.

Electronic gearing mechanics at SDC: how are gear ratios established and tuned in software — fixed ratio computed from mechanics, or tuned empirically per machine? And what instruction set do we actually standardize on — MAG for direct ratios, MAPC for position cam profiles, something else? What does the surrounding rung structure look like (engage/disengage sequencing, ratio staging, fault handling)?

Do we use camming (MAPC/MATC) or registration inputs (MAR) anywhere in current standards — and if so, for what class of application? If a job needs a nonlinear master/slave profile, is that an SDC-supported pattern or do we push the mechanics/vendor to solve it another way?

The standard axis module (the ~22-rung per-axis block): which rungs are pure boilerplate that never change, and which are the per-application ones? I read the staging rung, the wideband transition thresholds, and the permissive derivation as the application-dependent set — what else varies, and what should NEVER be touched per application?

Blending threshold judgment: when you pick the wideband (InPosWide) distance that lets the next axis start early, what are you actually computing — worst-case clearance geometry plus margin, or a tuned-on-the-machine value? And is there a class of corners you refuse to blend on principle even when the geometry technically clears?

The cycle currently ends at Cycle Complete after the next-cycle signal and restarts at the pick move — do you want an explicit internal loop-back edge instead, or is a supervisor-driven restart fine once this gets integrated?
